title: Per-feature capacity credits and hire-signal playbook
summary: A working sheet that ties per-feature capacity credits to staged hiring signals and price-sensitivity lanes. Intended for finance + product to operationalize roll-forward budgets and automated hire triggers when feature-level economics materially change.
body:
Objective:
- Provide a compact, actionable playbook that converts observed feature-level capacity burn and pricing elasticity into hiring signals (soft/hard) and budget re-allocations.

Scope and audience:
- Applies to hosted API product routes (generation, embeddings, chat) and feature add-ons (fine-tuned routes, reranking). Audience: finance, product leads, eng sprint leads, and solutions.

Why this approach:
- Historically Redwood uses coarse route-level budgets and manual HC conversations. This sheet creates a lightweight credit model: each feature consumes monthly "capacity credits" tied to token burn and tail-latency overhead. Credits expose marginal unit cost per feature and make hire signals less ad-hoc.

Concepts and definitions:
- Capacity credit: normalized monthly unit representing expected GPU-hours + operational overhead (one credit ~ $X cost baseline).
- Feature margin: revenue per credit - marginal cost per credit.
- Soft hire signal: advisory (60% confidence) prompting team planning and headcount prereqs.
- Hard hire signal: commit to posting/recruiting or contractor pool drawdown (90% confidence).

High-level flow:
1) Daily telemetry aggregates feature token burn and 7/30/90 day trailing growth rates.
2) Credits consumed = token_burn * credit_factor(feature_type) + overhead_credit(feature).
3) Map credits to marginal cost using latest GPU mix and quantization profile.
4) Recompute feature-level margin under three price lanes (base, -10%, -25%).
5) If margin breach crosses configured thresholds and growth persists, emit soft/hard hire signals and recommended price deltas or throttles.

Trigger matrix (summary):
- Table: (rows are signal types)
Signal | 30d growth | 90d growth | Margin drop vs baseline | Action
Soft   | >= 25%     | < 75%      | 15-25%                 | Planning note, reassign 0.5 FTE, run quantization experiment
Hard   | >= 40%     | >= 75%     | > 25%                  | Approve 1.0 FTE or contractor + pricing review
Buffer | any        | any        | margin < 8%            | Temporary price uplift test (+5-10%) or feature slab gating

Representative capacity-credit table (monthly view):
- Columns: feature, baseline credits, current credits, credits delta, marginal cost/credit, baseline price/unit, recomputed margin
- Example rows: 
"generation-standard": "base 12,000 credits | current 18,400 | +6,400 | $0.0028 | $0.015/token | margin 12% -> 6% under -10% price lane"
"search-embeddings": "base 3,200 credits | current 2,900 | -300 | $0.0015 | $0.009/embedding | margin 34% -> 30% under -10% lane"

Price-sensitivity lanes (used for scenario planning):
- Base: current published prices (assume no immediate changes).
- Defensive: a conservative drop in take-rate (-10%) to model competitive pressure or discounting.
- Aggressive compression: -25% take-rate to model slippage or price wars and large model-cost improvements.

Scenarios and recommended actions (mapped):
- Scenario A (high-growth, margin compression): 60% 30d growth, margin shrinks 30% under base -> Action: issue hard hire signal for infra + two-month contractor runway; initiate +7% price test for top 10% of traffic; enable prefix KV caching for affected route.
- Scenario B (steady growth, minor compression): 28% 30d growth, margin -12% -> Action: soft hire signal; prioritize batching/quantization ops; delay new hires pending 30d recheck.
- Scenario C (low growth, margin intact): <10% growth -> Action: no hire. Consider strategic discounts to recover uptake on low-margin features.

Runbook for finance/ops (quick steps):
1) Weekly ingestion: finance pulls feature credit usage, quantization profile, GPU mix, and list of active pricing tests.
2) Recompute marginal costs; populate monthly sheet and delta columns.
3) Automatic flags: send Slack channel #finance-hiring-alert with a short payload when a soft/hard trigger fires.
4) Product + Eng review: within 5 business days for soft triggers; 48 hours for hard triggers.
5) Execute mitigations: price tests, caching toggles, feature gating, contractor sourcing.

Hiring phasing guidance (sizing):
- 0.5 FTE (technical redirect): triage infra ops + batching improvements (expected to reduce credits by 10-15%).
- 1.0 FTE (mid-level infra engineer): ownership of autoscaling and quantization experiments.
- 2.0 FTE (senior infra + ML engineer): handle model-variant rollouts and kernel selection for long-term throughput wins.

Sensitivity calculations (example):
Inputs: credits_delta = 6,400; marginal_cost_per_credit = $0.0028; current revenue_per_credit = $0.015
Base margin = (0.015 - 0.0028) / 0.015 = 81%
If take-rate drops -10%: revenue_per_credit = 0.0135 -> margin = (0.0135 - 0.0028) / 0.0135 = 79% (absolute change small but scale matters)
If cost improves by 20% (quantization/spot mix): cost = 0.00224 -> margin improves to 83%

Open questions / caveats:
- Credit normalization constant must be reviewed quarterly to reflect hardware price shifts and other factors.
